Triage (R+148): lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` ⇒ `domain:services`. Graded `Bug` · `priority:p3` · `i18n`.

`Bug`: ruling D (2026-09-03) set the ladder as `sys_user.locale` → `Accept-Language` → deployment default, #14762 landed it at three sends, and this is the fourth — **the only send to an existing account still on the two-rung #14319 ladder**.

`priority:p3` — cosmetic, one mail template, no user report.

⭐ What makes it worth doing rather than shrugging is the shape of the inconsistency: a user who set `zh-CN` gets **Chinese password-reset mail and English magic-link mail from the same deployment**, decided by whichever browser happened to send the request. ⇒ *"The ladder is meant to be one answer per recipient, not one per callback."*

### ⭐ The fence that produced this card was correct

`sendMagicLink` is handed only `{ email, url, token }` — every other send gets a `user` object with an `id`. Reading the column needs a lookup keyed by **email**, *"a query shape the card did not name, on a path the card did not name"*. ⇒ Adding it silently would have been scope creep on a `p3`, and filing it was right.

The mechanism already exists: `AuthManager.storedRecipientLocale` takes an arbitrary `where`, so this is **a call site, not a mechanism** — one `findOne('sys_user', { where: { email }, fields: ['locale'] })` behind the existing placeholder-address refusal, threaded into `emailLocaleArg`'s stored parameter exactly as the other three do.

### ⚠️ The open question is real — answer it in the PR, ⛔ do not skip it

> a magic link is requested **BY the recipient**, so the request rung is legitimate here in a way it is not for an admin-initiated reset.

⇒ That is the strongest case in the family for leaving a send on the request rung, and the card is right to name it. ⚠️ **Ruling D still puts the stored column on top**, so the default is to implement — but if the lane concludes the magic-link path should keep `Accept-Language` first, that is a **narrowing of a maintainer ruling** and goes to the decision inbox, ⛔ not into a PR body.

⚠️ Measured on `origin/main` **after #14762's branch**. ⇒ Confirm #14762 has landed before starting; if it has not, the helper this depends on may not be there yet.

⛔ Out of scope: #14641 (invitations) is a separate rung with a separate reason.

## PM — PR #16062, and the card's headline survived measurement

`sendMagicLink` now reads the recipient's own `sys_user.locale` — the last of the five auth sends to reach the top rung of #14788's option-D ladder.

### ⭐ The enumeration was verified, not assumed, and it found a disagreement inside the card

The card's headline — *"the one auth mail to an existing user that still ignores `sys_user.locale`"* — **holds in both directions**. But the card's own body says *"the fifth auth send"* while its triage comment says *"this is the fourth"*, and the dev **resolved both rather than picking one silently**: there are five `sendTemplate` sites in `auth-manager.ts`, of which magic link was the **fourth to gain** the column and the **last one without** it.

The population is mechanism-anchored rather than keyword-guessed — `IEmailService` declares exactly two delivering members — with **three controls that fire**: `sendTemplate(` hits 16 files outside `plugin-auth` (so the pattern is not silently over-narrow); `.send(` inside `plugin-auth/src` returns three hits, all SMS (so no second mail mechanism exists); and the wired better-auth callback enumeration closes the surface at four email plus three SMS.

### ⭐ Reading the ruling at source paid, exactly as intended

I deliberately did **not** restate ruling D in the brief — this seat had already injected false statements into four briefs by carrying claims between documents. Reading it at source (#14788 comment 5522880441, maintainer verbatim 「同意」) turned up two things **neither the brief nor the card carries**: the ladder's order derives from **#14787's ruling B** (the column is a *user-stated preference*), and ruling D **inserts** the column above `Accept-Language` rather than replacing it.

⇒ That second point **answers the card's open question with no narrowing** — the request rung is kept, not replaced, and the recipient-requested nature of a magic link argues for keeping the header as the second rung, never for putting it above the column. **Nothing goes to the decision inbox.**

### ⛔ A correction to my brief, and to the card's framing

I called `sendMagicLink` *"the one … that still ignores `sys_user.locale`"*. True at filing and still true — but **the world moved underneath the card**: `f074616e6` (#15119) landed the invitation rung **after** this card was written, shrinking the set from two to one between filing and dispatch. ⇒ The card's fence-out reasoning about #14641 being "a separate rung" is now **historical**, not current. ⭐ A card is a reading of the tree at a moment; ⛔ its supporting reasoning ages even when its headline does not.

Also measured rather than assumed: the address is lowercased for the lookup because better-auth applies **no** case transform to the magic-link request body, while `findUserByEmail` — which `/magic-link/verify` resolves the same link with — matches on `email.toLowerCase()`. Both read in the **installed 1.7.2**.

### Verification

68 pins (51 + 17 new), package suite 102 files / 2157 tests, typecheck exit 0 with `tsc` echoed (⛔ not a zero-match zero) and the new file proven inside a checked program. **55 of 55** derived gates green, with the **Reconciliation** line read as the authority. Two answered exit **3 PREREQUISITE NOT MET** first — ⛔ recorded as neither red nor pass — then converted to real measurements after building the closure they named. Mutation with the fix **committed first**, restore proved by blob equality **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`; the RED quotes name the magic link falling back to the deployment default, and the predicate pin reporting *"no `sys_user` read happened at all"*.

⛔ Contract review **queued, not run** — the declared tier is rate-limited (probed five times, all 429 at launch). Nothing here is armed or landing until it passes.
